questions.stem: Ultrasound is defined as sound with a frequency:
questions.explanation: Ultrasound is any sound with a frequency above 20 kHz, which is above the upper limit of human hearing.

questions.stem: Medical ultrasound imaging is preferred over X-rays for scanning unborn babies because:

options.text: Ultrasound is non-ionising and safer for the baby
X-rays cannot pass through the body

questions.explanation: Ultrasound is non-ionising radiation, meaning it does not damage cells or DNA. X-rays are ionising and could harm the developing baby.

questions.stem: In ultrasound imaging, echoes are produced when ultrasound waves:

options.text: Reflect at boundaries between different materials or tissues

questions.explanation: Ultrasound pulses reflect at boundaries between materials of different densities. The reflected echoes are detected and used to build an image.

questions.stem: What device converts electrical signals to ultrasound waves and back again?
questions.explanation: A transducer converts electrical energy into ultrasound pulses and also detects the returning echoes, converting them back into electrical signals.

questions.stem: To calculate the distance to a reflecting boundary using ultrasound, you need to know:

options.text: The speed of ultrasound in the medium and the time for the echo to return
The frequency and wavelength of the ultrasound
The temperature of the medium only
The amplitude of the ultrasound pulse

questions.explanation: Distance = speed x time / 2. You divide by 2 because the ultrasound travels to the boundary and back, so the total distance is twice the actual depth.

questions.stem: Ultrasound can be used in industry to:

options.text: Detect cracks and flaws inside metal components

questions.explanation: Industrial ultrasound is used for non-destructive testing -- detecting internal cracks, voids, or flaws in metal components without cutting them open.

questions.stem: Why does ultrasound have very short wavelengths?

options.text: Because it has very high frequency, and wavelength = speed/frequency
Because it has very low energy
Because it only travels through solids

questions.explanation: From v = f x lambda, a very high frequency with a given speed results in a very short wavelength. This allows ultrasound to detect small features.
